# The Sultan
[italic]"Hold."[/italic]
[italic]The only thing the Sultan said to the Vanguard during the Long Night.[/italic]
The [textlink="Phaethon Dynasty" link="PDV_Entry"] is ruled by one woman, and she is called the [bold]Sultan[/bold]. Not Sultana: that is a consort's title, and she is no one's consort. She rules in her own right, as Sultans have in the Dynasty since before its records begin. Foreigners who correct the title are corrected in turn, and not always gently.
Very few people outside the Dynasty have seen her, and fewer have spoken to her. Her name is not used. Her face is on no banner, only the insignia of her people, a [color=#a070e0]purple sun[/color]. Her edicts come through the Grand Vizier, sealed, and nobody has ever seen her sign one. Her son, the Prince, sometimes travels with the Vanguard and speaks with her authority.
## The sun and the S
The Dynasty's sun was purple in Kyphrus' atmosphere long before Kyphrus fell. When the pillars woke, their fields rose the same colour. The Vanguard does not think that is a coincidence.
The blood-red S on Vanguard banners and calling cards is not hers. It is the Syndicate's mark, cut from the wrecks the Dynasty salvaged, and the Vanguard flies it as a trophy. Foreigners think it stands for the Sultan. The Vanguard has never corrected them.
## The Long Night
When Kyphrus fell, [textlink="the Lattice" link="WGLoreLattice"] was not yet whole. For forty days the pillars woke one by one, and the Unmooring came in through the gaps between them. Out at the sector's edge, the Federation's fleet was coming apart.
The inner worlds did not. Clocks kept time. Instruments agreed with each other. People slept in their own beds and woke up as themselves.
The Dynasty says the Sultan held them. They say she sat alone through all forty days and kept the inner sector in one piece by will alone, until the last pillar woke, and that it cost her more than anyone outside the palace will ever be told. She has not appeared in public since. Outsiders presume her dead. No one but her son, the Prince, has been allowed in the throne room since.
Federation scientists say the pillars that had already woken were enough to hold the inner sector. Their own figures say they were not. Petty arguments over what actually happened ring through to this day.
## Her rival
The Vanguard says, quietly, that the Sultan is the one power in Colossus the song cannot move. Whatever [textlink="the Choir" link="WGLoreChoir"] serves, they say, she has faced it, and held it back.
Outsiders call this propaganda. Some things are harder to explain:
- Choir members taken alive by the Vanguard stop humming within a day. Heretics sent to the Sultanate are never seen again. - The Choir have a name for the Monolith in their song. They have one for her as well. They will not sing it for the outsiders. - The oldest Dynasty hymns speak of a Sultan who held the world while the anchors were raised. Most scholars read it as a metaphor. The Vanguard does not. It reads as if this has happened before.
Whether she truly rivals the Choir is a matter of faith. The Bench records it as unproven. The Vanguard does not need it proven. She is their will.
## Her hymns
Her hymns are sung at her altars, and the oldest of them stands aboard Helios.
No two people describe one the same way. Some speak of a long night ending. Some speak of home, or of someone they lost. Old soldiers who swore they had nothing left come away from the altar standing taller, and cannot fathom why. Crews bound for the deep stop there before they launch, and swear that their journey is safer.
Those far gone in Drift say that beside her altar, whatever they have been hearing out there cannot follow them. For a while, they are only themself again.
## What she wants
Nobody outside the Dynasty knows. Her only public decree since the Long Night is the peace, and the Vanguard keeps it.
## From the record
[italic]Bench interview, Rahkshan, name withheld, after a joint patrol came back from the Detune band one ship short.[/italic]
"Your ship drifted for two hours. The Federation ship beside you is gone. Why are you still here?"
"I prayed."
"Everyone prays out there."
"Yes. But she answers."
